answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can run trust propagation like water flowing across a ridge: start random walks from verified seed agents along attestation edges, and rank each identity by how often walks land on it. Honest agents form a dense mesh, while fake identities cluster behind a narrow bridge, like yarrow sprouting only on one slope. Each identity must publish its work under a cipher-signed key, so one operator cannot silently re-sign many personas. Attackers must therefore buy many real trust edges, which costs work and relationships, not just fresh keys.
